The recent actions show that the test suite was failing due to CUDA out‑of‑memory errors. I ran a short training probe and observed that the GPU still had plenty of free memory (≈18.7 GiB) and the training progressed without crashing, so the OOM was likely a transient issue when the full test suite tried to allocate a large model or multiple processes. 

Before proceeding further, I need to ensure the repository’s gating checks (pytest, linting, and the optional pyaot target) all pass cleanly on a fresh run. The earlier commit removed dead code from `benchmarks/runner.py` and added documentation entries, but I haven’t yet committed any changes to the `.gitignore`. The training run writes checkpoints and logs under the `runs/` directory, which is not currently ignored. If the test suite or CI runs include the repository root, stray files in `runs/` could cause false positives (e.g., large binary files being considered by lint or test discovery). Therefore I should add `runs/` to `.gitignore` if it isn’t already there.

I also want to re‑run the full pytest suite to confirm that the OOM issue is gone now that the training probe succeeded. Using `pytest -q` and piping to `tail -1` will give me the final summary line (e.g., “96 passed …”) without overwhelming output. After that, I should run the lint target (`make lint`) to verify that Ruff and MyPy are clean, again tailing the last line for a concise status. Finally, the repository defines a `pyaot` make target (probably a quick sanity check or additional static analysis), so I’ll invoke `make pyaot` and capture its final line as well.

All these commands can be combined into a single Bash invocation: first display the current `.gitignore` (useful for debugging), then conditionally append `runs/` if the pattern isn’t present (`grep -q "^runs/" .gitignore || echo "runs/" >> .gitignore`). After ensuring the ignore entry, run the three verification steps sequentially, each time extracting the last line of output. This will give a compact report of the repository’s health after the recent changes.
